title: Interactive hotpatch protocol + safe deploy brain dump
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a messy brain dump for an interactive hotpatch protocol that lets us: (1) push tiny behavioral fixes to serving nodes without full rollout, (2) run live A/B tests against a patch, and (3) provide deterministic rollback and post-mortem artifacts if something goes sideways.

Constraints and non-goals:
- Must not violate running SLOs (latency P95 target 120ms) during common-case patches.
- Patches are limited to safe transformations: handler-level feature flags, small codelets (lua-ish), policy rules, quantization profile swaps, and model-weights pointer changes (no full-model upload in-band).
- Non-goal: full CI testing or model training pipeline. This is a runtime delivery mechanism for narrow fixes.

High-level actors:
- Developer (patch author): writes patch bundle and test harness.
- Patch Coordinator (control-plane service): validates, signs, stages, and coordinates delivery.
- Serving Node (runtime agent): accepts patch, runs sandboxed verification, applies to local process or spawns sidecar microworker.
- Canary Controller (client-side or control-plane): routes a subset of traffic to patched nodes for evaluation.

Desired properties:
- Signed bundles (integrity + provenance)
- Sandboxed / resource-limited execution of dynamic code (cpu/cgroup limits, mem caps)
- Can do gradual rollouts + automatic rollback on error budget/regression signals
- Observability: per-patch traces, diffs of traces vs baseline, sample requests/outputs stored for later replay

Example flow (happy path):
1) Author creates patch bundle and a tiny test harness (unit + smoke). Local sign + upload to control-plane.
2) Coordinator runs basic static checks (size, banned syscalls, matches policy).
3) Coordinator stages patch to N nodes (e.g., 5 nodes) as "candidate" and signals them to fetch bundle.
4) Each node: sandbox-verify -> run smoke harness with a small synthetic profile -> report metrics to Coordinator.
5) If all nodes pass, Canary Controller routes 1% traffic to candidates for 15min.
6) Telemetry + quality checks run (latency, error-rate, semantic regressions from sample prompt tests).
7) On success: patch is promoted to gradual rollout. On failure: immediate rollback, automatic debug capture (heap, traces, last requests).

Failure modes we must handle:
- Patch crashes runtime agent on startup -> node must automatically revert to last-known-good and escalate (ticket + alert).
- Patch causes subtle semantic regression -> signal via evaluation suite triggers rollback and keeps captured samples for postmortem.
- Coordinator becomes partitioned -> nodes continue running candidate in isolation but revert if they lose lease after TTL.

API shapes (rough drafts)
- PATCH bundle metadata (signed manifest) (fields are explanatory, not final):

{
  "bundle_id": "sha256:...",
  "author": "ava.thompson@redwood.com",
  "created_at": "2026-02-18T16:12:00Z",
  "description": "hotfix: kv-cache leak guard",
  "allowed_effects": ["handler_rewrite","policy_rule","config_toggle"],
  "signature": "sig-v1:...",
  "hashes": ["patch.lua:sha256:..."]
}

- Coordinator endpoints (control plane):
  - POST /v1/patches -> upload bundle (multipart: manifest + binary artifact)
  - GET /v1/patches/{id}/status -> candidate nodes + metrics
  - POST /v1/patches/{id}/promote -> rollout policy (percentages, windows)
  - POST /v1/patches/{id}/rollback -> immediate revoke and revert TTL

- Node agent contract (RPC over mTLS)
  - POST /agent/v1/patch/apply -> body: {bundle_id, manifest, fetch_url} -> returns: {status, verification_log_id}
  - GET /agent/v1/patch/{bundle_id}/verify -> returns verification result and smoke results
  - POST /agent/v1/patch/{bundle_id}/commit -> commit to runtime (atomic if possible)
  - POST /agent/v1/patch/{bundle_id}/revert -> revert to previous state

Sandboxing model (options we considered):
- Native process isolation + LD_PRELOAD shim to intercept syscalls (fast, but brittle across glibc/kernel versions)
- WASM runtime sandbox (good language isolation, deterministic resource accounting)
- Lua sandbox inside runtime (lightweight, already used in edge hooks)

NOTES: leaning towards WASM + constrained runtime for arbitrary codelets. Benefits: stronger isolation, consistent semantics across platforms, deterministic resource limit APIs. Downside: tooling burden for authors.

Instrumenting checks / metrics for safe rollout:
- Perf: p50/p95 token latency, CPU/VM usage, GC churn, mem high-water mark
- Correctness: embedding drift distance on a small prompt set, classifier/regression signals (e.g., toxicity score), smoke test success rate
- Safety: banned-io syscall attempts, sandbox escape attempts, excessive syscalls count

Sample rollout policy DSL (very rough):
- policy name: "canary-1pct-15m"
- steps: [
    {"percent": 1, "duration": "15m", "pass_if": "no_semantic_regressions && error_rate_increase < 0.1%"},
    {"percent": 10, "duration": "30m", "pass_if": "latency_p95_incr < 5ms && error_rate_increase < 0.2%"},
    {"percent": 100, "duration": "rolling", "pass_if": "manual"}
  ]

Operational playbook sketch:
- On alert: pause promotion, capture samples, open incident-runbook (auto-populate with patch bundle id + nodes).
- If revert required: coordinator issues revert -> nodes run revert -> subscribe to postmortem job that collects traces and diffs.
- Postmortem: attach signed bundle, smoke harness outputs, sample diff archive, and a short human writeup.

Integration notes with other Redwood systems:
- Console: new UI panel under "Deployments -> Hotpatches" showing feeds, signatures, and per-patch metrics
- Logging: use existing trace/span enrichment to attach patch.bundle_id to all requests handled under patch window
- Billing / Quota: patches should not create new billable resources automatically; any patch requiring new model weights must go through Reserved/Private deploy path.

Open questions / TODOs:
- AuthZ model: who can push what? scoped RBAC for sensitive patches (policy_routing, kms-changes).
- TTL semantics: how long can a candidate live if Coordinator is partitioned? Current thought: 5m lease + auto-revert unless explicitly promoted.
- Canary traffic selection: should be tenant-aware, region-aware, or request-profile-aware?
- Snapshotting: how do we reliably capture pre-patch request context for diffs without exploding storage? sample rate + heuristics?
- Runtime memory snapshot hooks: do we allow heap dump on revert? cost/risks?

Quick prototype next steps (1-2 week spike):
- Implement a minimal Controller endpoint to accept signed bundles and store them in S3-like store + metadata db (spike only, no HA).
- Implement a tiny node-agent in go that fetches a wasm bundle, runs it in Wasmtime with cpu/memory limits, and executes a smoke harness (HTTP replay).
- Instrument metrics + a simple console page to show candidate nodes and wire up Canary Controller to route small percent traffic (nginx / envoy weight change via control-plane API).

Sketch: component interaction (ASCII)

  Author -> Coordinator (POST bundle)
                  |
                  v
        +--------------------------+         +------------------+
        |  Patch Coordinator (CP)  |<------->|  Monitoring / ML |
        +--------------------------+         +------------------+
           |      |    ^                          ^
           |      |    | push / status            | alerts / regression signals
           |      v    |                          |
  fetch -> +--------+  |  lease                 +------+
           | Node A |<-+------------------------| NODES|
  smoke -> +--------+  |  revert/commit         +------+
           |  wasm  |  |
           +--------+  |
                       |
                       v
                 Canary Controller -> Traffic Router (Envoy)

Notes to self: keep this doc short and iteration-friendly. We need to sync with SRE (Ravi) about rollback UIs and with privacy/legal on sample retention before we wire auto-capture. Schedule 30m sync with Kai + SRE next Tues.

Other random ideas:
- Allow patch bundles to carry a small deterministic replay suite (fuzzes + golden outputs) so nodes can run reproducible semantic checks offline.
- Provide a "read-only preview" mode where patch can be evaluated on live requests but not affect outputs (shadow-run path) and capture predicted vs actual diffs.

-- end of dump --
